cta.heading: Does your brand look as credible as your product?
cta.body: Show us your current brand, website and deck. In 30 minutes we'll tell you whether you need a refresh, a new identity or a full repositioning.

sections.heading: Brand strategy
sections.answer: Brand strategy defines who the company is for, what it stands for, and why a buyer should believe it, before any logo is drawn. It is the brief that every visual and verbal decision is checked against.
body: For a technology company that usually means a sharp positioning statement, a clear category, the proof that backs the claim, and a tone of voice that fits the people who buy.

sections.heading: Positioning
paras: Positioning decides what you want to be known for, and against whom. A crowded category punishes vague positioning: if a buyer cannot repeat what you do in one sentence after visiting your site, the brand is not doing its job.
We test positioning against how buyers actually describe their problem, in sales calls, reviews and search queries, so the words on the website match the words in the buyer's head.

sections.heading: Visual identity
items: Logo system: primary, secondary and favicon versions
Colour: palettes that work on screen and meet accessibility contrast
Typography: type that holds up in headlines, product UI and documents
Iconography and illustration: a consistent visual language
Imagery direction: what photography and graphics should and shouldn't look like
Brand guidelines: how to use everything, so partners and new hires keep it consistent

sections.heading: Digital brand systems
paras: A modern brand has to work in software as well as on a slide. We translate identity into design tokens and components, so the same colours, type and spacing drive the website, the product and marketing assets.
This is where branding and product design meet. It is also why technology brands built only for print tend to fall apart the first time an engineer has to apply them. See design systems.

faq.q: How much does startup branding cost?
faq.a: It depends on how much strategy and research the brand needs and how far the identity has to extend (website, product, collateral). We quote against a written scope. Our startup branding cost guide explains typical scopes in India.

faq.q: What should a startup branding package include?
faq.a: At minimum, positioning, a logo system, colour, typography and guidelines that tell others how to use them. Funded technology startups usually also need a digital brand system and website direction so the brand works in the product.

faq.q: How long does a branding project take?
faq.a: A brand strategy and visual identity project typically takes four to eight weeks, depending on the number of revision rounds and decision-maker availability.

faq.q: How should a B2B SaaS company approach rebranding?
faq.a: Start with what is not working and what equity you have: what customers recognise and value. Reposition first, then evolve the identity, then roll it out across website, product and documents in a planned sequence.
We can, but for a technology company a logo alone rarely solves the problem. Positioning and a usable system matter more than the mark.

faq.q: Can you also design our website and product UI?
faq.a: Yes. Brand, website and product design are done by the same senior team, which keeps the brand consistent where buyers actually meet it.
